offline_proof.statement: The core flow and ingress cases prove deterministic topic validation, routing, payload serialization, and rejection diagnostics.

The validator proves package-local paths, UTF-8 text, link resolution, rejection of known secret signatures and credential-field patterns, and preflight rejection of network-capable test behavior before focused checks execute.
The coverage contract proves required module IDs, surface classifications, claim ownership, source resolution, and freshness metadata.

The node capability fixtures prove exact source-owned identity, authentication-family separation, bounded transaction and polling decisions, topic validation, and acknowledgement-stage distinctions for the pinned offline contracts.

cannot_prove.statement: Offline assets cannot prove IAM, resource-principal authorization, broker, device-host, Object Storage, database, queue, Notifications, File Storage, or external endpoint reachability.

Offline assets cannot prove lifecycle completion, software updates, managed palette availability, adapter normalization, history, logs, metrics, events, subscriber delivery, or effective deployed state.
No package check authorizes or performs live operations, mutation, command delivery, notification publication, replay, deployment, or cleanup.
Pinned sample-package behavior and deterministic cases cannot prove a node or dependency is installed, permitted, compatible, authenticated, reachable, or effective in a selected Flow Runtime.

managed_target_selection.contract: Source-role classification is independent of target selection. Target selection binds exact runtime provenance, palette node type, module identity/version, and affirmative contract evidence for fields, outputs, authentication, and provenance. Verified evidence can plan a bounded managed test only; it cannot assert live compatibility, acceptance, or authorization.
